issues.legal_issue: Income from family property allotted to members for their enjoyment remains income of the family when the arrangement provides only for maintenance and the income is applied to discharge the family’s maintenance obligation.
material_facts: A Hindu undivided family entered into a family arrangement under which properties were placed in the possession of certain male members for their enjoyment and maintenance.

The arrangement did not disrupt the family’s joint status, give the members absolute rights in the properties, or provide for devolution of those properties; the properties remained family property and could return to the family’s management.
The arrangement could be revised if the family’s circumstances substantially changed.
The family remained responsible for maintaining its members and for other family obligations, and the members used the income from the allotted properties for their maintenance.
The arrangement relieved the family of the expense of maintaining those members, and the members received and applied the income on behalf of the family.
issues.conclusion: The income from the allotted properties was deemed to be the family’s agricultural income and was includible in its taxable income.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 9(1) of the Kerala Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1950, agricultural income arising to another person from assets that remain the settlor’s or disponer’s property is deemed to be the settlor’s or disponer’s income. The provision is similar to section 16(1)(c) of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922. Applying the test in Commissioner of Income-tax, Bombay City v. Sitaldas Tirathdas, income applied after receipt to discharge the assessee’s obligation remains assessable, whereas income diverted by an overriding charge before it reaches the assessee is not. Raja Bejoy Singh Dudhuria v. Commissioner of Income-tax, Bengal was explained as a case of diversion by an overriding charge; P. C. Mullick v. Commissioner of Income-tax, Bengal was applied to distinguish application of received income. Commissioner of Income-tax, Bombay v. Makanji Lalji and Commissioner of Income-tax, Bombay City v. Ratilal Nathalal were also referred to.

rule.if: family_income_tax_assessment and assets_remain_family_property and arrangement_provides_only_maintenance and arrangement_is_revisable_on_substantial_change and allotted_income_is_applied_to_family_maintenance and family_is_relieved_of_maintenance_expense

predicates.family_income_tax_assessment: A tax assessment concerns income claimed to belong to a family.
predicates.assets_remain_family_property: The property producing the income remains owned by the family despite being placed in members’ possession.
predicates.arrangement_provides_only_maintenance: The family arrangement gives members enjoyment of property for maintenance without giving them absolute rights in it.
predicates.arrangement_is_revisable_on_substantial_: The arrangement can be changed if the family’s circumstances substantially change.
predicates.allotted_income_is_applied_to_family_mai: Members use income from the allotted property to maintain themselves under the family arrangement.
predicates.family_is_relieved_of_maintenance_expens: The arrangement relieves the family of an obligation to maintain the members receiving the income.

issues.definition: When a family income tax assessment concerns family-owned property placed with members only for maintenance, and its income discharges a maintenance obligation from which the family is relieved, the rule treats that income as includible family income.
